editions.title: Hottest Right Now
editions.headline: AI Design Hottest Right Now · Sunday, Oct 18, 2026
editions.summary: This was the week the code-first design fight went three-way. For a month the hottest AI design work has been animation, 3D and UI written as code by Claude Opus 5.5, and the month's most-saved design post is simply a list of the open-source repos that make it work. Then Gemini 4 Argon arrived on Oct 13 and several of its most-shared launch demos were design work: an exploded-view product film built in Blender from a raw CAD file, a 3D-printing CAD studio in Canvas, and a camera you can play like a synth. Four days later DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 landed as an open model, and within a day creators were racing it against Opus and Argon on the same motion-graphics prompts for a fraction of the cost. On the image side the open models kept coming, and the ComfyUI builds of FLUX 3 Image Klein and MOSS-Image are each past 330,000 downloads. What it means: the skill that matters is giving a model good taste, references and a way to check its own work, because the models themselves are getting cheaper and easier to swap.

editions.title: Best of the Day
editions.headline: AI Design Best of the Day · Sunday, Oct 18, 2026
editions.summary: The loudest design story of the weekend is DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, an MIT-licensed open-weights update that creators spent two days pitting against Claude Opus 5.5 on code-built motion graphics, 3D scenes and frontends. The announcement is the most-engaged AI post in today's sweep by a wide margin, the model sits at the top of Hugging Face's trending list, and one of the big AI video platforms called it "the new SOTA for motion design" after running its own tests. It matters because the hottest design technique of the month, motion and 3D written as code instead of rendered by a video model, has so far meant paying for a frontier model. If a free, open model holds up, that whole way of working gets much cheaper and can run on your own hardware. The verdict isn't settled, though: side-by-side tests are mixed, and a few came out with blown-out colours.

editions.title: AI Design in Use
editions.headline: A car that didn't exist, a house no one opened in Blender, and 102 clips that all passed QA
editions.summary: Standard Chartered is an official F1 partner with no F1 team, so the 2026 car in its new film 'Move Ahead' never existed. Co-director Marcello Costa drew it by hand, had AI turn the sketch into 3D and extrapolate the angles, and placed every decal with the agency. He calls single-detail edits 'like 50-50' and says full AI isn't automatically cheaper. That's this edition's pattern: the work that holds up starts with a human draft, locks references, and checks the output, whether it's a bank ad, an archviz set or a dragon boss.

editions.title: AI Design Daily
editions.headline: An open model just walked into the motion-design studio
editions.summary: DeepSeek released V4.1-Flash-1017 with MIT weights on Oct 17, and within hours creators were running it against Opus 5.5 on code-built motion graphics, 3D scenes and frontends. Around it: a 25-minute anime written entirely as code, MOSS-Image becoming Reddit's favourite open base model, and solo game builders settling on a repeatable method. 77 verified items from the last day.

editions.title: Hottest Right Now
editions.headline: AI Design Hottest Right Now · Saturday, Oct 17, 2026
editions.summary: The big story of the week and the month is the same one: the hottest AI design work is being made as code you can edit, not as pixels you regenerate. Figma's Config India launch put real website code on the canvas as Code Layers, the most-saved 3D posts have Claude write Python that builds every Blender model piece by piece, and a month of motion-design clips came from code-only animation with no video model at all. Meanwhile the image race got crowded and cheap fast: Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo, Nano Banana 2.1, FLUX 3 Image Klein and Krea 3 all landed within ten days, and the open-weights ones are already running in ComfyUI. The practical takeaway is that taste files, scripts and design systems are becoming the thing a designer actually owns.

editions.title: Best of the Day
editions.headline: AI Design Best of the Day · Saturday, Oct 17, 2026
editions.summary: The idea people kept saving today is a change in how 3D gets made. Instead of sculpting, creators have Claude Opus 5.5 write Python that builds each model part by part inside Blender, then rerun the script when something needs to change. A how-to thread on exactly that became one of the day's most-saved design posts, a case study of a Steam game built this way is circulating widely, and a steady stream of first-timers posted their own "vibe-modeled" assets within hours. It matters because it turns 3D from a craft skill into something you can direct, version and fix by editing a number, which is a different job for designers, not just a faster one.

editions.title: AI Design in Use
editions.headline: How people actually used AI design tools this week: 94 real uses
editions.summary: A solo developer shipping a Steam fishing game didn't model anything by hand: one Claude Code session wrote and ran Blender scripts for every crab, gull and palm. A crab went from a four-sentence brief to animated on the beach in 53 minutes. That's this edition's pattern: the people getting real results use AI as a scriptable crew they direct, check and correct, not as a slot machine.

editions.title: AI Design Daily
editions.headline: Open image models had the week, and agents learned to drive Blender
editions.summary: FLUX 3 Klein, Krea 3 and MOSS-Image all landed within about 24 hours, Kling 4.0 went global, and the most-bookmarked creative technique of the week was Claude Opus 5.5 building 3D models through Blender MCP. 87 verified items from Oct 10–17.
